input.command: cd /work; ls; curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/denisseram/dataset-snapshots/3731e02e38c75e5d70ae92bf3596a69951866c2d/ubuntu.csv | head -60; Rscript -e 'library(ggtime); print(ls("package:ggtime"))'

cd /work; cat > plot.R <<'EOF'
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggtime); library(ggplot2); library(readr); library(dplyr); library(tidyr)
})
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/denisseram/dataset-snapshots/3731e02e38c75e5d70ae92bf3596a69951866c2d/ubuntu.csv"
# Ragged rows: trailing missing fields become NA
raw <- suppressWarnings(read_csv(url, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                                 show_col_types = FALSE))
d <- raw |>
  mutate(across(created:`eol-legacy`, as.Date),
         type = ifelse(grepl("LTS", version), "LTS releases", "Interim releases"),
         type = factor(type, levels = c("LTS releases", "Interim releases"))) |>
  arrange(release) |>
  mutate(version = factor(version, levels = rev(version)))

yrs <- function(x, ref) as.numeric(x - ref) / 365.25
std_end <- d$eol
srv_end <- pmax(d$eol, d$`eol-server`, na.rm = TRUE)

phases <- bind_rows(
  tibble(d[c("version", "type")], phase = "Development",    start = d$created, end = d$release),
  tibble(d[c("version", "type")], phase = "Standard support", start = d$release, end = std_end),
  tibble(d[c("version", "type")], phase = "Extended server support", start = d$eol,
         end = ifelse(!is.na(d$`eol-server`) & d$`eol-server` > d$eol, d$`eol-server`, NA) |> as.Date()),
  tibble(d[c("version", "type")], phase = "ESM", start = srv_end, end = d$`eol-esm`),
  tibble(d[c("version", "type")], phase = "Legacy support", start = d$`eol-esm`, end = d$`eol-legacy`)
) |>
  filter(!is.na(start), !is.na(end), end > start) |>
  left_join(select(d, version, release), by = "version") |>
  mutate(x0 = yrs(start, release), x1 = yrs(end, release),
         phase = factor(phase, levels = c("Development", "Standard support",
                                          "Extended server support", "ESM", "Legacy support")))

events <- bind_rows(
  tibble(version = d$version, type = d$type, event = "Created (dev. start)", x = yrs(d$created, d$release)),
  tibble(version = d$version, type = d$type, event = "Release", x = 0)
)
today <- Sys.Date()
future <- d |> mutate(x = yrs(today, release)) |> select(version, type, x)

# Pattern for caption, computed from data
std_len <- d |> mutate(s = yrs(eol, release)) |> group_by(type) |>
  summarise(med = median(s), max_total = median(yrs(pmax(eol, `eol-server`, `eol-esm`, `eol-legacy`, na.rm = TRUE), release)))
lts_std <- std_len$med[std_len$type == "LTS releases"]
int_std <- std_len$med[std_len$type == "Interim releases"]
lts_tot <- max(phases$x1[phases$type == "LTS releases"])
cap <- sprintf(paste0("Aligned on release, releases share the same ~6-month development lead-in, but life cycles split in two: ",
                      "interim releases get ~%.0f months of standard support (median), while LTS releases get ~%.0f years ",
                      "and, since 14.04, ESM and legacy support stretching to %.0f years."),
               int_std * 12, lts_std, lts_tot)

pal <- c("Development" = "#9AA5B1", "Standard support" = "#2A78B5",
         "Extended server support" = "#5BB0A0", "ESM" = "#E39B3C", "Legacy support" = "#B5455A")

p <- ggplot(phases) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = x0, xend = x1, y = version, yend = version, colour = phase),
               linewidth = 3.2, lineend = "butt") +
  geom_point(data = future, aes(x = x, y = version), shape = "|", size = 3.2, colour = "black") +
  geom_point(data = events, aes(x = x, y = version, shape = event), size = 1.8,
             fill = "white", colour = "black", stroke = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal, name = "Phase", drop = FALSE) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Created (dev. start)" = 21, "Release" = 23), name = "Event") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-1, 16, 1), expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
  facet_grid(type ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Ubuntu release life cycles aligned on each release date",
       subtitle = sprintf("One row per release, ordered by release date (newest at top). Black tick = today (%s); dates beyond it are planned.", today),
       x = "Years relative to release date (0 = release)", y = NULL,
       caption = cap) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(linewidth = 4)),
         shape = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
        legend.position = "top", legend.box = "horizontal",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 10.5),
        plot.title.position = "plot", plot.caption.position = "plot")

ggsave("plot.png", p, width = 1400 / 150, height = 900 / 150, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
ggsave("plot.svg", p, width = 1400 / 150, height = 900 / 150, bg = "white")
EOF
render plot.R

content.text:
I've written `plot.R`, which saves `plot.png` and `plot.svg`; `render` runs it with no errors. The answer to the question is no. Once aligned on their release dates, releases split into two clearly different life cycles. They are alike only in their first six months: every release spends about six months in development before release.

- **Interim releases:** about 9 months of standard support (median). Up to 12.10 it was about 18 months.
- **LTS releases:** about 5 years of standard support. 6.06–10.04 also had extended server support to about 5 years. 12.04 added ESM to 7 years, and from 14.04 on, ESM plus legacy support runs to 15 years.

The caption numbers are computed from the data. The figure also shows a tick for today on releases still in their life cycle; everything to its right is planned.

```
REPORT
deliverable: plot.R
requirements:
  R1: done - one row per release, version as label, ordered by release date (oldest at top)
  R2: done - x = years since own release date (0 = release), axis "Years relative to release date"
  R3: done - colour-coded interval bars for development, standard, extended server, ESM, legacy, with legend; missing phases not drawn
  R4: done - created (circle) and release (diamond) point markers on each row
  R5: done - separate LTS / interim facets
  R6: done - title plus one-sentence caption, its numbers computed from the data
assumptions:
  - Extended server support drawn only when eol-server > eol; ESM starts at max(eol, eol-server)
  - Years = days / 365.25
  - Release order is oldest at top, within each facet
  - Ragged rows read with readr; missing trailing fields become NA (parse warnings suppressed)
limitations:
  - ggtime has no interval or event geoms for relative time; bars and markers are plain ggplot2 geom_segment/geom_point (ggtime is loaded but its mixtime scales do not fit a numeric relative axis)
  - The today tick uses the system date, so it moves depending on when the script runs
  - Future dates (planned EOL/ESM/legacy) are drawn like past ones; only the today tick separates them
  - Row labels are small (7 pt) to fit 47 releases in 900 px
```
